claim: Dop1R1 and Dop2R encode the D1- and D2-like receptors, respectively, in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: In the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, Dop1R1 and Dop2R encode the D1- and D2-like receptors, respectively, and are reported to oppositely regulate intracellular cAMP levels.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Dop1R1 and Dop2R oppositely regulate intracellular cAMP levels.
source: In the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, Dop1R1 and Dop2R encode the D1- and D2-like receptors, respectively, and are reported to oppositely regulate intracellular cAMP levels.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Both Dop1R1 and Dop2R dopamine receptors are detected at presynaptic and postsynaptic sites in multiple cell types.
source: We detected dopamine receptors at both presynaptic and postsynaptic sites in multiple cell types.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by imaging data in Figures 4-7.

claim: Both Dop1R1 and Dop2R are enriched at presynaptic sites.
source: Quantitative analysis revealed enrichment of both receptors at the presynaptic sites, with Dop2R showing a greater degree of localization than Dop1R1.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative data in Figures 3-7.

claim: Dop2R shows a greater degree of presynaptic localization than Dop1R1.
source: Quantitative analysis revealed enrichment of both receptors at the presynaptic sites, with Dop2R showing a greater degree of localization than Dop1R1.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative comparisons in Figures 3D and 7E.

claim: Presynaptic localization of Dop1R1 and Dop2R in dopamine neurons suggests dual feedback regulation as autoreceptors.
source: The presynaptic localization of Dop1R1 and Dop2R in dopamine neurons suggests dual feedback regulation as autoreceptors.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by imaging data in Figure 7.

claim: Starvation induces bidirectional modulation of presynaptic receptor expression in PAM and PPL1 dopamine neuron clusters.
source: Furthermore, we discovered a starvation-dependent, bidirectional modulation of the presynaptic receptor expression in the protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) and posterior lateral 1 (PPL1) clusters, two distinct subsets of dopamine neurons, suggesting their roles in regulating appetitive behaviors.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative data in Figure 8.

claim: Starvation increases Dop1R1 expression in PAM neuron terminals.
source: We found a significant elevation of Dop1R1 in the terminals of PAM-γ5 upon starvation for 10 hr or longer (Figure 8B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantitative data in Figure 8B-C.

claim: Starvation does not increase Dop2R in PAM-γ5 but rather tends to decrease it.
source: In contrast, starvation did not increase Dop2R in PAM-γ5 but rather tended to decrease, if at all (Figure 8B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantitative data in Figure 8B-C.

claim: Starvation increases Dop2R, but not Dop1R1, in PPL1-α3 neurons.
source: Strikingly, the starvation-induced changes in the PPL1 neurons were opposite to those in the PAM: Dop2R, but not Dop1R1, was significantly increased in the α3 compartment (Figure 8E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantitative data in Figure 8E-F.

claim: D1-like receptors are coupled with Gαs and activate adenylate cyclase upon ligand binding in mammals.
source: In mammals, D1-like receptors are coupled with Gαs, thereby activating adenylate cyclase upon ligand binding, whereas Gαi-coupled D2-like receptors inhibit cyclase activity (Beaulieu and Gainetdinov, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: D2-like receptors are coupled with Gαi and inhibit adenylate cyclase activity in mammals.
source: In mammals, D1-like receptors are coupled with Gαs, thereby activating adenylate cyclase upon ligand binding, whereas Gαi-coupled D2-like receptors inhibit cyclase activity (Beaulieu and Gainetdinov, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Four dopamine receptors have been identified in Drosophila: Dop1R1, Dop1R2, Dop2R, and DopEcR.
source: Four dopamine receptors have been identified in Drosophila: Dop1R1, Dop1R2, Dop2R, and DopEcR (Han et al., 1996; Hearn et al., 2002; Srivastava et al., 2005; Sugamori et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Dop1R1 and Dop2R are also known as DopR1, dDA1, and dumb, and as DD2R, respectively.
source: Dop1R1 and Dop2R, also known as DopR1, dDA1, and dumb, and as DD2R, respectively, correspond to the D1- and D2-like receptors, respectively (Hearn et al., 2002; Sugamori et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Dop1R2 and DopEcR are invertebrate-specific and recruit different second messenger systems.
source: Dop1R2 and DopEcR are invertebrate-specific and have been reported to recruit different second messenger systems (Han et al., 1996; Srivastava et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Expression of dopamine receptors is highly overlapping in the fly brain.
source: Intriguingly, recent data of single-cell RNA-seq and transgenic expression profiling revealed that the expression of these dopamine receptors is highly overlapping in the fly brain (Croset et al., 2018; Davie et al., 2018; Kondo et al., 2020), unlike the spatially segregated expression of the D1- and D2-like receptors in vertebrate brains (Gerfen and Surmeier, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: D1- and D2-like receptors have spatially segregated expression in vertebrate brains.
source: Intriguingly, recent data of single-cell RNA-seq and transgenic expression profiling revealed that the expression of these dopamine receptors is highly overlapping in the fly brain (Croset et al., 2018; Davie et al., 2018; Kondo et al., 2020), unlike the spatially segregated expression of the D1- and D2-like receptors in vertebrate brains (Gerfen and Surmeier, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Kenyon cells encode a variety of sensory information.
source: Kenyon cells (KCs), the major MB intrinsic neurons, encode a variety of sensory information (Honegger et al., 2011; Turner et al., 2008; Vogt et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Each Kenyon cell receives synaptic inputs from different dopaminergic projections in multiple spatially segmented compartments along its axon in the MB lobe.
source: Intriguingly, each KC receives synaptic inputs from different dopaminergic projections in multiple spatially segmented compartments along its axon in the MB lobe (Aso et al., 2014a; Tanaka et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: MB-projecting dopamine neurons originate from three cell clusters.
source: MB-projecting dopamine neurons (DANs) originate from the three cell clusters (Mao and Davis, 2009; Nässel and Elekes, 1992).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: DANs in the PPL1 cluster project to the vertical lobes and the peduncle of the MB.
source: DANs in the protocerebral posterior lateral 1 (PPL1) cluster project to the vertical lobes and the peduncle of the MB, and they control different aspects of associative memory (Aso et al., 2010; Aso et al., 2012; Aso and Rubin, 2016; Claridge-Chang et al., 2009; Krashes et al., 2009; Mao and Davis, 2009; Masek et al., 2015; Riemensperger et al., 2005; Takemura et al., 2017; Vogt et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: PPL1 DANs control different aspects of associative memory.
source: DANs in the protocerebral posterior lateral 1 (PPL1) cluster project to the vertical lobes and the peduncle of the MB, and they control different aspects of associative memory (Aso et al., 2010; Aso et al., 2012; Aso and Rubin, 2016; Claridge-Chang et al., 2009; Krashes et al., 2009; Mao and Davis, 2009; Masek et al., 2015; Riemensperger et al., 2005; Takemura et al., 2017; Vogt et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: The PAM cluster is the largest DAN cluster and mostly projects to the medial lobes of the MB.
source: The protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) cluster, the largest DAN cluster, mostly projects to the medial lobes of the MB, and many PAM neurons are involved in reward processing (Burke et al., 2012; Felsenberg et al., 2018; Huetteroth et al., 2015; Ichinose et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2012; Yamagata et al., 2015; Yamagata et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Many PAM neurons are involved in reward processing.
source: The protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) cluster, the largest DAN cluster, mostly projects to the medial lobes of the MB, and many PAM neurons are involved in reward processing (Burke et al., 2012; Felsenberg et al., 2018; Huetteroth et al., 2015; Ichinose et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2012; Yamagata et al., 2015; Yamagata et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: DANs in PPL2ab project to the MB calyx and control the conditioned odor response.
source: DANs in PPL2ab project to the MB calyx and control the conditioned odor response (Boto et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Kenyon cells express all four dopamine receptor subtypes.
source: In addition to the variety of the dopamine sources, KCs express all four dopamine receptor subtypes (Deng et al., 2019; Kondo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Lobe-projecting DANs have synaptic outputs to multiple types of neurons, including MBONs, APL, and DPM.
source: Besides KCs, these lobe-projecting DANs have synaptic outputs to multiple types of neurons, including MBONs, APL, and DPM (Li et al., 2020; Takemura et al., 2017; Zhou et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Both Dop1R1-T2A-GAL4 and Dop2R-T2A-GAL4 labeled many neuropils including the MB.
source: Both lines labeled many neuropils including the MB (Figure 1A and B), and the overlapping expression of these receptors is consistent with our previous quantification of GAL4-positive cells for both genes (58,049 and 68,528 for Dop1R1 and Dop2R, respectively, out of 118,331 brain cells; Kondo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1A-B.

claim: Dop1R1 and Dop2R are co-expressed in Kenyon cells.
source: We confirmed the co-expression of Dop1R1 and Dop2R in the KCs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) as reported previously (Kondo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The PAM cluster of DANs expressed both Dop1R1 and Dop2R.
source: The PAM cluster of DANs expressed both Dop1R1 and Dop2R (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1C-D.

claim: Most DANs in the PPL1 cluster strongly expressed Dop2R, but Dop1R1 only weakly.
source: On the other hand, most of the DANs in the PPL1 cluster strongly expressed Dop2R, but Dop1R1 only weakly (Figure 1C and E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1C and E.

claim: Dop1R1, but not Dop2R, was highly expressed in the ring neurons projecting to the ellipsoid body.
source: We further found that Dop1R1, but not Dop2R, was highly expressed in the ring neurons projecting to the ellipsoid body (Figure 1G and H; Hanesch et al., 1989) and the neuropil ensheathing glia (Figure 1I; Awasaki et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1G-H.

claim: Dop1R1, but not Dop2R, was highly expressed in the neuropil ensheathing glia.
source: We further found that Dop1R1, but not Dop2R, was highly expressed in the ring neurons projecting to the ellipsoid body (Figure 1G and H; Hanesch et al., 1989) and the neuropil ensheathing glia (Figure 1I; Awasaki et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Dop1R1 and Dop2R genes are co-expressed in PAM neurons and KCs but have selective expressions in other cell types.
source: In conclusion, Dop1R1 and Dop2R genes are co-expressed in PAM neurons and KCs but have selective expressions in other cell types.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Memory scores of the rGFP-fused receptor flies were comparable to that of control flies without GFP11 insertion.
source: Memory scores of the rGFP-fused receptor flies were comparable to that of control flies without GFP11 insertion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dop1R1 and Dop2R are required for aversive memory in α/β and γ KCs.
source: Both Dop1R1 and Dop2R have been shown to be required for aversive memory in α/β and γ KCs (Kim et al., 2007; Scholz-Kornehl and Schwärzel, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations to prior work.

claim: Dop1R1 and Dop2R proteins are distributed throughout KC membranes with predominant enrichment in the lobes.
source: These receptors were distributed throughout KC membranes with predominant enrichment in the lobes (Figure 3A–C), but sparsely in the calyx (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: Dop1R1 and Dop2R are sparsely distributed in the calyx of KCs.
source: These receptors were distributed throughout KC membranes with predominant enrichment in the lobes (Figure 3A–C), but sparsely in the calyx (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3B-C.

claim: Enrichment in the lobes was more pronounced in Dop2R compared to Dop1R1.
source: LI quantification revealed that enrichment in the lobes was more pronounced in Dop2R compared to Dop1R1, whereas localization to the calyx was sparser in Dop2R than Dop1R1 (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Localization to the calyx was sparser in Dop2R than Dop1R1.
source: LI quantification revealed that enrichment in the lobes was more pronounced in Dop2R compared to Dop1R1, whereas localization to the calyx was sparser in Dop2R than Dop1R1 (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: KC-specific visualization of Dop1R1 and Dop2R proteins revealed signals around the Brp puncta of the same cells, suggesting presynaptic localization.
source: Interestingly, KC-specific visualization of Dop1R1 and Dop2R proteins revealed signals around the Brp puncta of the same cells, suggesting presynaptic localization (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B-C.

claim: Receptor condensates were found adjacent to the Brp clusters of non-KCs, suggesting their localization at the postsynaptic sites.
source: Additionally, we found the receptor condensates adjacent to the Brp clusters of non-KCs, suggesting their localization at the postsynaptic sites (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B-C.

claim: The synaptic receptor localization is consistent in different subsets of KCs (α/β and γ).
source: The synaptic receptor localization is consistent in different subsets of KCs (α/β and γ; Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Both Dop1R1 and Dop2R are enriched in the presynaptic and postsynaptic sites of KCs.
source: In conclusion, both of these antagonizing dopamine receptors are enriched in the presynaptic and postsynaptic sites of KCs (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results and illustrated in Figure 4D.

claim: Not all Brp puncta of KCs were associated with the dopamine receptors.
source: Interestingly, we found that not all Brp puncta of KCs were associated with the dopamine receptors (Figure 5A), suggesting that dopaminergic presynaptic modulation is heterogeneous across release sites.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Dopaminergic presynaptic modulation is heterogeneous across release sites in KCs.
source: Interestingly, we found that not all Brp puncta of KCs were associated with the dopamine receptors (Figure 5A), suggesting that dopaminergic presynaptic modulation is heterogeneous across release sites.
evidence: This is stated in the results and inferred from data in Figure 5A.

claim: Giant neurons exhibit characteristics of mature neurons, including firing patterns.
source: Importantly, these giant neurons exhibit characteristics of mature neurons, including firing patterns (Wu et al., 1990; Yao and Wu, 2001; Zhao and Wu, 1997) and acetylcholine release (Yao et al., 2000), both of which are regulated by cAMP and CaMKII signaling (Yao et al., 2000; Yao and Wu, 2001; Zhao and Wu, 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations to prior work.

claim: Giant neurons exhibit acetylcholine release regulated by cAMP and CaMKII signaling.
source: Importantly, these giant neurons exhibit characteristics of mature neurons, including firing patterns (Wu et al., 1990; Yao and Wu, 2001; Zhao and Wu, 1997) and acetylcholine release (Yao et al., 2000), both of which are regulated by cAMP and CaMKII signaling (Yao et al., 2000; Yao and Wu, 2001; Zhao and Wu, 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations to prior work.

claim: Brp was localized to the terminals of neurites in giant neurons, but rarely in the proximal neurites.
source: In the giant neurons from the Brp::SNAP embryos (Kohl et al., 2014), Brp was localized to the terminals of neurites, but rarely in the proximal neurites (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Punctate Brp clusters were found in the giant neuron terminals.
source: Furthermore, we found punctate Brp clusters in the giant neuron terminals (Figure 5B), together recapitulating the essential characteristics of the AZ cytomatrix in adult neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Both Dop1R1 and Dop2R were expressed in the giant neurons and enriched in the same distal axonal segments.
source: Both Dop1R1 and Dop2R were expressed in the giant neurons and enriched in the same distal axonal segments (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Dop1R1 and Dop2R are associated with the Brp clusters in giant neurons.
source: A closer investigation revealed that these receptors are associated with the Brp clusters (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The presynaptic localization of dopamine receptors is independent of the circuit context.
source: These observations in the giant neurons are strikingly similar to those in the KCs (Figures 3—5A), corroborating that the presynaptic localization of these receptors is independent of the circuit context.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on comparison of data from KCs and giant neurons.

claim: MBON-γ1pedc>αβ has most of its postsynaptic sites on the γ1 compartment and the peduncle of the α/β neurons.
source: MBON-γ1pedc>αβ (also known as MB-MVP2, MBON-11; Aso et al., 2014a; Tanaka et al., 2008) has most of its postsynaptic sites on the γ1 compartment and the peduncle of the α/β neurons and send axonal projections to the α and β lobes (Figure 6; Dorkenwald et al., 2023; Schlegel et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations to prior work and shown in Figure 6.

claim: Both Dop1R1 and Dop2R are enriched in the dendritic projection of MBON-γ1pedc>αβ in the γ1 compartment.
source: Strikingly, both Dop1R1 and Dop2R are enriched in the dendritic projection in the γ1 compartment (Figure 6B and C) in sharp contrast to the sparse distribution of these receptors in the dendrites of KCs (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6B-C.

claim: Dop1R1 and Dop2R were detected in the presynaptic boutons of MBON-γ1pedc>αβ.
source: Additionally, we detected these receptors in the presynaptic boutons (Figure 6C), which are consistent with the results in KCs and in the giant neurons (Figures 4B, C, 5A and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: D2-like receptors in mammals are expressed in DANs and act as autoreceptors.
source: D2-like receptors in mammals are expressed in DANs and act as autoreceptors, which mediates feedback signals by receiving neurotransmitters released from the neuron on which the receptors reside (Ford, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation to prior work.

claim: Multiple dopamine receptor genes are expressed in Drosophila DANs.
source: In Drosophila, multiple dopamine receptor genes are expressed in DANs (Figure 1D and E; Aso et al., 2019; Deng et al., 2019; Kondo et al., 2020), but it is unclear if these receptors function as autoreceptors.
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations and shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: PAM neurons are polarized with presynaptic proteins abundantly enriched in the MB lobe and barely detected in dendrites.
source: The PAM neurons are polarized; presynaptic proteins are abundantly enriched in the MB lobe and barely detected in dendrites (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7A-B.

claim: Both Dop1R1 and Dop2R were localized to the terminals in the MB lobes of PAM neurons.
source: We visualized Dop1R1 and Dop2R proteins in the PAM cluster DANs using R58E02-GAL4, and both were localized to the terminals in the MB lobes (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Dop2R showed stronger presynaptic enrichment than Dop1R1 in PAM neurons.
source: Representation of LI for Dop1R1 and Dop2R in the PAM neurons again showed stronger presynaptic enrichment of Dop2R than Dop1R1 (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Dop2R was strongly enriched at β'1 compartment showing significantly higher LI than Dop1R1.
source: Dop2R was strongly enriched at β'1 compartment showing significantly higher LI than Dop1R1 (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7D-E.

claim: Both Dop1R1 and Dop2R accumulate in the boutons of PAM neurons.
source: Higher magnification revealed the accumulation of both Dop1R1 and Dop2R in the boutons (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7F.

claim: The presynaptic localization of Dop1R1 and Dop2R in DANs suggests that both receptors mediate feedback regulation.
source: The presynaptic localization of Dop1R1 and Dop2R in DANs suggests that both receptors mediate feedback regulation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on the localization data.

claim: The activity of MB-projecting DANs is dynamic and sensitive to feeding states.
source: The activity of MB-projecting DANs is reported to be dynamic and sensitive to feeding states (Ichinose et al., 2017; Liu et al., 2012; Plaçais and Preat, 2013; Senapati et al., 2019; Siju et al., 2020; Tsao et al., 2018; Yamagata et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations to prior work.

claim: Starvation for 10 hr or longer significantly elevated Dop1R1 in the terminals of PAM-γ5.
source: We found a significant elevation of Dop1R1 in the terminals of PAM-γ5 upon starvation for 10 hr or longer (Figure 8B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 8B-C.

claim: Starvation enhances presynaptic dopamine signaling in the reward-related PAM neurons by shifting the balance of Dop1R1 and Dop2R.
source: These results together suggest that starvation enhances presynaptic dopamine signaling in the reward-related PAM neurons by shifting the balance of Dop1R1 and Dop2R.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on the starvation data.

claim: Dop2R proteins were detected in all MB projections of the PPL1 neurons.
source: We detected Dop2R proteins in all MB projections of the PPL1 neurons, whereas Dop1R1 proteins were only detectable in the terminals of the PPL1-α3 neuron (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Dop1R1 proteins were only detectable in the terminals of the PPL1-α3 neuron.
source: We detected Dop2R proteins in all MB projections of the PPL1 neurons, whereas Dop1R1 proteins were only detectable in the terminals of the PPL1-α3 neuron (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Starvation induces bidirectional modulation of the dual autoreceptor system in the PPL1 and PAM DANs.
source: Taken together, starvation induces bidirectional modulation of the dual autoreceptor system in the PPL1 and PAM DANs, and we propose that these changes shift the balance of dopamine output from these subsets (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results and illustrated in Figure 9A.

claim: Dopaminergic signals from the PPL1 neurons inhibit expression of appetitive olfactory memory in fed flies.
source: The dopaminergic signals from the PPL1 neurons inhibit expression of appetitive olfactory memory in fed flies (Krashes et al., 2009; Pavlowsky et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations to prior work.

claim: Increased Dop2R autoreceptors in starved flies may disinhibit appetitive memory expression by suppressing PPL1 outputs.
source: The increased Dop2R autoreceptors in starved flies (Figure 8E and F) may thus disinhibit appetitive memory expression by suppressing PPL1 outputs (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and illustrated in Figure 9B.

claim: Appetitive memory was impaired by transgenic knockdown of Dop2R specifically in the PPL1 cluster neurons.
source: Indeed, appetitive memory was impaired (Figure 9C), suggesting the significance of the negative feedback regulation of the PPL1 via Dop2R in appetitive behavior expression.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Enhanced negative feedback to PPL1 via Dop2R in the starved state contributes to the expression of appetitive behavior.
source: This result is consistent with our model, which suggests that enhanced negative feedback to PPL1 via Dop2R in the starved state contributes to the expression of appetitive behavior (Figure 9A and B).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results and illustrated in Figure 9A-B.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9-based insertion is advantageous in terms of flexibility in fusion sites compared to intronic insertions of reporters using transposons.
source: Compared to intronic insertions of reporters using transposons (Fendl et al., 2020), CRISPR/Cas9-based insertion is advantageous in terms of flexibility in fusion sites (Bonanno et al., 2024; Kamiyama et al., 2021; Sanfilippo et al., 2024; Williams et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: C-terminal tagging of dopamine receptors does not perturb protein localization and function.
source: This enables the C-terminal tagging of dopamine receptors that do not perturb protein localization and function (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The split-GFP reconstitution strategy enables sensitive detection of low-abundant endogenous proteins by the tandem multimerization of the GFP11 tags.
source: The split-GFP reconstitution strategy enables sensitive detection of low-abundant endogenous proteins by the tandem multimerization of the GFP11 tags, as shown in other epitope tags such as SunTag and smFPs (Tanenbaum et al., 2014; Viswanathan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: The native fluorescence of rGFP was sufficient to detect tagged proteins at the high signal-to-noise ratio, without the need for signal amplification using antibodies.
source: The native fluorescence of rGFP was sufficient to detect tagged proteins at the high signal-to-noise ratio, without the need for signal amplification using antibodies.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the experimental observations.

claim: The background fluorescence of the split-GFP fragments was practically negligible.
source: The background fluorescence of the split-GFP fragments was practically negligible (Figure 8D; Kamiyama et al., 2016; Kondo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by Figure 8D and citations.

claim: Released dopamine is not confined to the synaptic cleft, but diffused in the extracellular space.
source: Released dopamine is not confined to the synaptic cleft, but diffused in the extracellular space (Liu et al., 2021; Rice and Cragg, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: Volume transmission can increase the number of target synapses by 10 times.
source: Such volume transmission can increase the number of target synapses by 10 times (Li et al., 2020; Takemura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: The broader distribution of Dop1R1 may enable it to respond to extrasynaptic dopamine.
source: Thus, the broader distribution of Dop1R1 (Figures 3B–D–7C–E) may enable it to respond to extrasynaptic dopamine.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Dop2R at the AZ may inhibit activities of adenylate cyclases and voltage-gated calcium channels in response to residual dopamine.
source: In response to residual dopamine, Dop2R at the AZ may inhibit activities of adenylate cyclases and voltage-gated calcium channels (Beaulieu and Gainetdinov, 2011; Hearn et al., 2002), thereby reducing the noise of the second messengers.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: The spatial configuration of Dop1R1 and Dop2R may enhance the sensitivity and precision of dopaminergic modulation.
source: Collectively, the spatial configuration of Dop1R1 and Dop2R may enhance the sensitivity and precision of dopaminergic modulation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion based on the localization data.

claim: Presynaptic receptor localization suggests a spatially confined cAMP, forming nanodomains.
source: Furthermore, presynaptic receptor localization (Figures 4B–D—7F) suggests a spatially confined cAMP, forming nanodomains (Anton et al., 2022; Bock et al., 2020; Maiellaro et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: cAMP signaling regulates multiple events at presynaptic terminals, such as the molecular assembly at the AZ and synaptic vesicle dynamics.
